pr_title: Remove locks from COM events delegate management.
pr_body:
This removes locks and instead assumes the collection is immutable.

Fixes #73754

issue_context.title: COM event with recursion .net 6 problem
issue_context.body:
### Description

We are using a system that exposes UI interface using COM objects. It is an external application so I cannot send a minimal reproduction source code of a problem.  I will try to explain the whole workflow.

#### Background information

There is an application interface (COM) that exposes event.

Event declaration in the App interface:

```c#
event _IApplicationEvents_StatusBarEventEventHandler StatusBarEvent;
```

Delegate definition:

```c#
public delegate void _IApplicationEvents_StatusBarEventEventHandler([In][MarshalAs(UnmanagedType.BStr)] string Text, [In] BoStatusBarMessageType messageType);
```

There is also a StatusBarControl that allows us to set up the ProgressBarMessage:

```c#
application.StatusBar.SetText(“some text”);
```

When we set the text to the status bar Event is fired.

### Reproduction Steps

UseCase: When the StatusBarEvent fires with text equal to “crush” we want to change this to "****" on the status bar

EventHandler implementation:

```c#
public override void OnStatusBarDisplayed(string text, BoStatusBarMessageType messageType)
{
    if (text.Equals("crush",StringComparison.CurrentCultureIgnoreCase))
    {
        application.StatusBar.SetText("*****");
    }
}
```

I will provide some screenshots of the debugging session:

1. Set "crush" to the status bar. ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11562129/183669932-142a27de-d396-46d6-af17-028fabef3b5c.png)
2. We get the Event notification and call the setText("****").
3. System freezes. We can see that the event handler thread freezes on the set text method. ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11562129/183670295-a1fd1989-ec16-44db-88b8-9276995fca18.png)
4. We can see that in the separate thread invoking a method the foreach loop of _delegateWrapper. ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11562129/183670408-a912b540-42d3-401b-abe8-633cb8b21d7d.png)

### Expected behavior

What should happen: this thread @29816 should invoke this method and Call the OnStatusBarDisplayed event again. This is working correctly when running in the .net framework.

Below is the same call stack of the .net framework debugging session. ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11562129/183670717-228d0842-c11f-49f4-ae78-182c29f6afe6.png)

Calling SetText in another thread is not an option for us.


### Actual behavior

System freezes. We can see that the event handler thread freezes on the set text method. ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11562129/183670295-a1fd1989-ec16-44db-88b8-9276995fca18.png)

### Regression?

This is working correctly when running in the .net framework.

### Known Workarounds

Calling SetText in another thread but this is not an option for us.

### Configuration

.NET 6.0
Windows 11
x64


### Other information

_No response_

review_comments: Mainly I'm curious: are enough COM events subscribed to by multiple delegates in order to warrant this optimization of using Delegate.Combine rather than just having each delegate be its own entry in the list?  It looks safe from a cursory inspection, but it's a lot easier to prove correctness when the list being used is entirely immutable, whereas here the published list instance is having its contents modified.

I honestly don't know. This was a direct port from .NET Framework, aside from the list locking I added. I'm hesitant to change anything in the logic just because the COM events scenario is so uncommon and the generally low familiarity with all the user scenarios. I can add this to the backlog for investigation but I don't think it is worth changing in this PR.

I think there is a bug when `Remove` is called on two threads in parallel:

First thread starts creates a new array with the delegate removed
Second thread removes the delegate in-place without creating a new array
First thread swaps in its array, reverting the affect of the second remove.

> I think there is a bug when Remove is called on two threads in parallel:

Yeah, this is an example of the kind of issue that comes from trying to get sneaky (I hadn't noticed this particular case, but you're right about the bug).

I think it'd be better to just do the simple thing and actually have the list be immutable; then the only concurrency management need be the simple act of publishing safely.  Plus you get the added benefit of the code being much simpler / easier to maintain.

Or if our goal is to stick with what netfx had, just revert the locking entirely and go back to exactly what netfx had :)
